title: KP-2A UAM airframe

source.original_file: Content/KP2A/KP2A_Blueprint.uasset, the blueprint that composes the vehicle from its fuselage, wing, booms, tilt rotors, gear and lights (UE 5.2 copy; the DTAMFramework copy is saved by UE 5.5)
source.note: The operator's own airframe, exported from the blueprint they fly rather than from KP2StaticMesh. That static copy carries 101 placeholder Automotive Materials slots and renders blue, and the KP2A skeletal mesh on its own is only the control surfaces and gear.

rights.label: operator-owned
rights.credit: AeroDT operator / DTAM project (materials carry KADA and VIBUM logos)
rights.note: Confirmed by the operator as their own asset on 2026-09-09, so AeroDT may publish it. Third-party marks inside the liveries (KADA, VIBUM) belong to their owners.

scale_basis: export bounding box 7.75 (X, longitudinal) x 4.12 (Y, vertical) x 10.18 (Z, span), treated as metres because the source is the operator's own model and the proportions match a UAM of this class; not checked against a drawing
forward_axis: unverified (longitudinal axis is X; nose direction not established)
conversion_note: Exported part by part from the blueprint, each mesh component replaced by an actor at the same world transform with the same material overrides, because exporting the blueprint actor itself writes the node tree without geometry. The body carries MI_CarPaint_White and the canopy MI_Glass_Windshield_Tinted, so the livery is the operator's own rather than a placeholder. Six internal battery components were left out: they are 85% of the source triangles and are never seen from outside. The remaining static meshes were reduced to 30% and exported from that level of detail; materials were baked to 512 px sets.
